text:
ash: Quick sync: thinking about a lightweight header `X-Auth-Scope` to disambiguate routing for service accounts. Keeps routing explicit instead of inferring from key claims. Thoughts?
sophie: Useful. Is this header intended to change billing attribution or only routing/telemetry?
ash: Start with routing + telemetry + soft quotas. Billing remains tied to the key's billing_project until org opts in.
matt: Security: if clients can set it, we must validate via per-key allowed scopes claim or ACL. Otherwise it's elevation.
ash: Agreed. Flow: gateway reads header -> auth service verifies allowed_scopes -> audit event if override used. Reject (403) when not allowed.
billing-liz: For finance add `resolved_scope` and `scope_override` to export lines so downstream reconciles usage. We'll need a migration window.
sophie: Also a read-only `X-Auth-Scope-Audit` to let clients test without affecting routing. Good for telemetry during rollout.
svcbot: Note: schedule canary flag `auth-scope-v1` -> canary 5% at 2026-04-10T10:00Z.
matt: Telemetry: add labels `scope_source` = {claim, header, audit_only} and `scope_override_key`. Dashboard: override_ratio per org + signature failure count if any.
ash: Rate limiting: enforce per-key limits first, then coarse scope-level shaping. Keep low-cardinality tiers to avoid metric explosion.
sophie: Console: per-key toggle "Allow scope header overrides" and recent override log. Admins can opt keys in/out.
billing-liz: CSV export fields: `resolved_scope`, `scope_overrode`, `billing_project`. We'll communicate change to billing consumers.
ash: Action items: @matt implement gateway + auth check, @sophie add telemetry & console copy, @billing-liz handle export. Keep default audit-only until metrics look good.
matt: I'll open a PR with tests for allowed_scopes validation.
sophie: I'll create Grafana skeleton for scope_override_rate and an FAQ blurb.
ash: Thanks. Conservative rollout and clear audit logs.
